title: The Fishburne Formation (Lower Eocene), a newly defined subsurface unit in the South Carolina coastal plain
citation: Gohn, G.S. Hazel, J.E., Bybell, L.M., and Edwards, L.E., 1983, The Fishburne Formation (Lower Eocene), a newly defined subsurface unit in the South Carolina coastal plain: U.S. Geological Survey Bulletin 1537-C, map scale 1:875,000.
reader: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), trial reading in the build session, 2026-10-03
notes:
Depths are below kelly bushing as measured from geophysical logs (page 11 footnote: for CC1 subtract 5 ft to get core depths of Gohn and others, 1977). Microfossil species lists (pages 12, 14) are not recorded as values. Figures 1-5 (pages 8, 13, 15, 17, 20) are mostly unreadable as text; page 17 (figure 4) has no text. References: only those about South Carolina or the Atlantic Coastal Plain stratigraphy are recorded; general paleontology and zonation references (Bukry, Costa and Downie, Enright, Hardenbol and Berggren, Hazel 1969, Loeblich and Tappan, Martini, Olsson, Owens and Minard, Stainforth and others, Gibson and others) are skipped.
Depths are below kelly bushing as measured from geophysical logs (page 11 footnote: for CC1 subtract 5 ft to get core depths of Gohn and others, 1977). Microfossil species lists (pages 12, 14) are not recorded as values. Figures 1-5 (pages 8, 13, 15, 17, 20) are mostly unreadable as text; page 17 (figure 4) has no text. References: only those about South Carolina or the Atlantic Coastal Plain stratigraphy are recorded; general paleontology and zonation references (Bukry, Costa and Downie, Enright, Hardenbol and Berggren, Hazel 1969, Loeblich and Tappan, Martini, Olsson, Owens and Minard, Stainforth and others, Gibson and others) are skipped.
